# Step 7: Gene Annotation with Prokka

Prokka was used to identify genes within the 14 selected metagenomic bins and predict their possible functions. It does this by comparing the identified gene sequences with previously characterised genes and their known functions. This provides a better understanding about what microorganisms, associated with black band disease, may be capable of doing. 

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Test Prokka on one selected bin
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/prokka

bin=metabat.5
prokka --cpus 2 --outdir $bin --prefix $bin ../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa

# Examine the annotation files
ls metabat.5
```

## Annotating All Selected Bins

After Prokka was successfully tested on one bin, a SLURM job was submitted to identify and annotate genes across all 14 selected metagenomic bins.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Submit Prokka job
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/prokka
sbatch run_prokka.sh

# Check job status
squeue -u $USER
```

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Check Prokka job completion
sacct -j 624 --format=JobID,State,ExitCode

# Examine annotation results
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/prokka
ls metabat.26
head -n 10 metabat.26/metabat.26.tsv
```

The Prokka analysis completed successfully and produced annotation files for the 14 bibns that contain predicted gene names and function. These included predicted genes with known functions, as well as hypothetical proteins because their function could not be determined.
